video.title: Make $1K an Hour With This Simple Side Hustle

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Wesley, owner of a Grounds Guys franchise in Keller, Texas (DFW), about adding a Christmas lights installation line to a lawn business. They cover pricing by linear foot, a leasing model where the operator keeps and stores the lights, rising margins in repeat years, labour and time per job, insurance, marketing (door hangers, Facebook, yard signs) and low startup costs. Wesley claims one Grounds Guys owner does $1.25M in Christmas lights alone. Key takeaway: recurring, route-dense, leased holiday lighting can have high repeat-year margins, but it is physical, risky work that agents cannot do.

speakers.name: Wesley
speakers.description: Owner of Grounds Guys of Keller (DFW, Texas), three years into holiday lighting

speakers.name: Jeremy
speakers.description: Production manager at Grounds Guys, manages crews and customer communication

ideas.name: Residential Christmas light installation (leased lights, recurring annual)
ideas.one_liner: Install, store and remove custom-fit Christmas lights on homes each year, leasing the lights to customers and earning higher margins on repeat years.
ideas.business_model: Annual per-job install fee priced per linear foot; lights leased and owned by the operator; yearly recurring with 10% discounts in years 2 and 3.
ideas.customer: Homeowners in larger homes (example 3-4,000 sq ft house) wanting roofline lights without doing it themselves.
ideas.problem: Hanging lights is risky, time-consuming and fiddly; homeowners must store and fix lights and replace bulbs.
ideas.offer: Professional measured, custom-cut roofline lighting, timer included, installed, serviced if bulbs fail, taken down and stored by the company.

pricing.model: Per linear foot of roofline, with a minimum job; 10% discount in year 2 and again in year 3, then flat.
pricing.notes: Permanent lighting is 2-3x the price. Customer-owned lights model priced differently. No extra charge for colour changes (Wesley says they could charge).

acquisition_channels.details: Door hangers delivered by install crews to a 'box nine' of nearby homes (2 each side plus 5 opposite) while working, creating two touch points.

quote.text: we call it box nine. So, we'll do the two homes on each side, two homes on that side, and the five homes opposite side of the street.
quote.speaker: Wesley

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook posts with before and afters plus Facebook marketing are the main lead generation.

quote.text: Facebook posts or Facebook we'll do our own posts, you know, before and afters as well as the Facebook marketing.
quote.speaker: Wesley

acquisition_channels.details: Yard signs (now technically illegal in Texas this year per Wesley); another franchisee put out about 80 signs a month and accepted complaints for the leads.

Marketing to the internal CRM of existing lawn customers and taking over commercial customers from another Grounds Guys; campaigns start in July (early-bird discounts) and again late September/early October.
Repeat customers rarely reshop if communication is good; idea of knocking on doors of new owners of homes where lights are already cut to fit (not yet tried).

ideas.delivery: Measure with a measuring wheel, pre-bulb and pre-clip socket wire in the shop (30-60 min), two-person crew (one on ladder/roof, one on ground) installs in 1-1.5 hours for a large house; takedown takes about 10 minutes with painter's pole; strands labelled and stored indoors; service calls for failures. Employees do installs.
unit_economics_claims: Year-one margin about 20-25%, year three about 50-60%
ideas.startup_cost: $400-500 minimum for materials plus safety gear/ladders; $2-3k typical first year; Wesley spent $4.5-5k on material for about 15 homes.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Same season; marketing starts July, installs in Oct-Nov (supply ships around September).

acquisition.how: Facebook ads, before/after posts, seasonal email/CRM to existing customers can be agent-run. Door hangers and yard signs are physical and legally awkward.

onboarding.how: Quotes need physical measuring of the roofline on site (could be approximated with satellite imagery tools, not stated).

delivery.how: Two people on ladders and roofs install, service and take down lights; entirely physical.

billing.how: Annual invoicing and renewal with fixed discount schedule is easily automated.

support.how: Scheduling updates and enquiries can be agent-handled, but service call dispatch is physical.

uk_applicability.notes: Demand is strong in the US where big house Christmas displays are a norm; UK is much smaller market and lower display culture, houses often smaller with fewer large rooflines, shorter ladders work and Work at Height Regulations, public liability insurance and PAT/electrical safety apply. UK PECR would restrict cold targeting but door hangers/leaflets are fine.

risks: Falls from roofs and ladders, serious injury
Higher insurance rates for risky activity
Hard to find staff willing to go on roofs
Squirrel damage, service calls on single bulbs

tactics.name: Lease-and-store lights for repeat revenue
steps: Cut lights to fit the house and keep ownership
Store lights indoors between seasons
Discount 10% in year 2 and 3, then hold flat
Reuse material for new customers if one cancels
Margin rises from about 20% to 50-60% by year 3

quote.text: We cut the lights and we keep the lights and we're essentially leasing them to them.
quote.speaker: Wesley

tactics.name: Price by linear foot after wheel measurement
steps: Measure roof lines from the ground with a measuring wheel
Account for roof pitch with simple maths
Apply a per-linear-foot price
Apply minimum job around $800

quote.text: We use a measuring wheel. So we'll just basically walk it off from here.
quote.speaker: Wesley

tactics.name: Pre-bulb in the shop and design for easy takedown
steps: Pre-bulb and pre-clip wire on spools in the shop
Use minimal time on site
Install so takedown can use a painter's pole without ladders
Label strands and keep a sketch of runs
Mark peaks with coloured zip ties

tactics.name: Box nine door hanger marketing
steps: When installing at one home, hang door hangers on 2 homes each side and 5 opposite
Neighbours see the crew and get a second touch point

tactics.name: Seasonal marketing calendar
steps: Run campaigns in July with early-booking discounts
Restart marketing late September/early October
Take down from second week of January

tactics.name: Route density scheduling
steps: Give customers a one-week install window
Route areas together for install and takedown
Cluster to avoid driving time exceeding job time

tactics.name: Proactive communication on mistakes
steps: Crews call immediately after incidents like hitting a mailbox
Manager calls the customer first
Be available any time of day

tactics.name: Target new owners of homes with pre-cut lights
steps: When a customer moves, knock on the new owner's door
Offer lights already fit to the house at a deeper discount

tools_mentioned.name: Home Depot
tools_mentioned.purpose: Not recommended; lights not made for custom fit

warnings.warning: Falling from roofs is a serious risk; prioritise safety training and equipment.

quote.text: watch videos on safety. Um, because that's the number one thing.
quote.speaker: Jeremy

warnings.warning: Make sure staff will actually go on roofs before hiring; several hires backed out.

quote.text: hire someone to get on the roof.
quote.speaker: Wesley

warnings.warning: Never hire uninsured roof workers; insurance classes this as higher risk.
Texas recently made yard signs technically illegal; neighbours may complain.
Avoid installing high up where adjustments or timers need a ladder; each service call for one bulb is costly.

lessons.lesson: Recurring, repeat-year work increases margin because material is already paid for and install time drops.
Route density determines profit: drive time can exceed on-site time.
Communication and proactive honesty keep customers from reshopping.

quote.text: communication covers a multitude of sins.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Seasonal add-on lines can diversify a thin-margin base business like mowing.
Owning the asset (leasing lights) creates switching costs and lets you resell to new owners.
Start small and test on your own house; the downside is a ladder.

quote.text: The worst you could do is have a ladder that you get to keep for your house now.
quote.speaker: Wesley

lessons.lesson: Commercial customers can be worth far more than residential ones.
Price in risk and insurance cost; the liability is part of what the customer pays for.
Physical risky field work is a poor fit for agent-run businesses, but pricing, scheduling and marketing parts can be automated.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific prices, margins and costs, but only three years in, no revenue totals for his own lights business, and the $1.25M claim is hearsay. Setting is a Grounds Guys franchise in Texas.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes his paid community (tkowners.com); guest promotes Grounds Guys franchise.
